title: In Zechariah 9 How Does The Prophecy Of Judgment Against Israels Enemies Encourage Believers Today
paragraphs: Understanding Zechariah 9: Judgment and Hope

The ninth chapter of Zechariah is a remarkable blend of prophecy, warning, and encouragement. It opens with pronouncements of judgment against the nations surrounding Israel and crescendos into a message of hope, highlighting the arrival of a humble King. For believers today, this chapter provides deep encouragement by showcasing God’s sovereignty, His justice, and His unwavering faithfulness to His people.
1. The Context: God’s Sovereignty Over the Nations

Zechariah 9 begins with a series of oracles against Israel’s traditional enemies—Hadrach, Damascus, Tyre, Sidon, Ashkelon, Gaza, and Ekron. These nations were known for their wealth, strength, and opposition to God’s people. God’s message is clear: He alone is sovereign over all nations.
The burden of the word of Jehovah upon the land of Hadrach, and Damascus shall be its resting-place (for the eye of man and of all the tribes of Israel is toward Jehovah)... - Zechariah 9:1 ASV

The phrase “the eye of man and of all the tribes of Israel is toward Jehovah” indicates that God’s dealings with the nations are in full view of His people, reminding them that He alone determines the fate of kingdoms and rulers.
2. God Judges the Proud and Delivers the Humble
A significant section of the prophecy focuses on Tyre, a city famed for its wealth and fortifications:

And Tyre did build herself a stronghold, and heaped up silver as the dust, and fine gold as the mire of the streets. Behold, the Lord will dispossess her, and he will smite her power in the sea; and she shall be devoured with fire. - Zechariah 9:3-4 ASV

This passage demonstrates that no amount of human achievement or pride can stand against the Lord’s purposes. God’s judgment on Israel’s enemies serves as a warning against pride and a comfort that evil will not prevail indefinitely.
3. God Protects His People
God’s justice is paired with His gracious protection of Israel:
And I will encamp about my house against the army, that none pass through or return; and no oppressor shall pass through them any more: for now have I seen with mine eyes. - Zechariah 9:8 ASV
This promise reassures believers that God is not distant or indifferent. He actively watches over and defends His people, ensuring that even in the midst of judgment, His own are secure.
4. The Coming King: The Ultimate Encouragement
The most famous portion of Zechariah 9 is the prophecy of the coming King, fulfilled in Jesus Christ:

Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee; he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, even upon a colt the foal of an ass. - Zechariah 9:9 ASV

This humble entry points directly to Jesus’ triumphal entry into Jerusalem (Matthew 21:5 ASV). It reminds believers that God’s deliverance comes not through might or violence, but through the humble and saving work of Christ.
5. How Does This Encourage Believers Today?
God’s Justice Will Prevail: In a world where evil often seems to go unchecked, Zechariah 9 assures believers that God will judge the nations and hold the wicked accountable (Psalm 37:28 ASV).
God Is Faithful to His People: God’s promise to encamp around His house reassures us of His ongoing protection and care (Romans 8:31 ASV).
Christ Is Central: The prophecy of the coming King points us to Jesus, reminding us that our ultimate hope and encouragement are found in Him (Colossians 1:18 ASV).
God’s Kingdom Is Unshakable: The defeat of Israel’s enemies foreshadows the final victory of God’s kingdom over all opposition (Revelation 21:4 ASV).
Conclusion

Zechariah 9 is a powerful reminder that God is both just and merciful. He judges the proud, delivers the humble, and brings ultimate hope through the coming of Christ. For believers today, this passage is a call to trust in God’s sovereign plan, rejoice in His protection, and fix our eyes on the humble King who brings salvation.
